title: the tree tool names itself the one graph-tree tool every learning block uses
intention: cairn/tools/tree/tree.py and its charter say what the tool is: the one graph-tree tool every learning block uses to work the trees the librarian delegates to it, not chart's; a learning block that needs a special adaptation subclasses it.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: cairn/tools/tree/tree.py's module docstring opens 'chart/tree.py — the TREE STRATUM: the orient nexus's own graph tree' and calls itself 'Stone 2 of the chart device' and 'that rung for chart's nexi'; OWNER = 'chart' at tree.py:61 is the default owner. Users: build_inspector/nexus.py and tools/orient/nexus.py pass owner explicitly; codemother's orient, deposit, survey, constrain, triage, validate, hypothesize and decompose call deposit_learning with no owner (eight; seed_trees and watch pass owner='codemother'), so their leaf rows land in chart_<nexus>_nodes tables; ticket 2b3d842bc118 moves them to codemother_<nexus>_nodes. Akien 2026-11-05 (Q#54, outline 19.29): 'i think it's stated as belonging to the chart because that was the first time we defined it at that level, but it's the same tool everywhere. if learning blocks need a special adaptation of it in some way, then it'd be a subclass.' And: 'so add it as part of the build plan'.
traces_to: Law 5 (the address tells a cold reader what the tool is now), Law 1 (Q#54 is settled; the code must not re-teach the old answer).
how: Rewrite the module docstring of cairn/tools/tree/tree.py (lines 1-50) to open: the one graph-tree tool every learning block uses (outline 19.29, Q#54, Akien 2026-11-05), first defined at this level for chart, reaching each holder's own table through the librarian's published trees tool; keep the verbs section; add that a special adaptation is a subclass and that OWNER = 'chart' is the default the codemother callers lean on. Change no code line. Update the charter's what/why through `cairn artifact write --verb write`. Red-first proof over the docstring (ast.get_docstring) and the charter.
falsifier: (1) tree.py's module docstring names cairn/tools/tree/tree.py as the one graph-tree tool every learning block uses, cites outline 19.29 (Q#54), and contains none of 'chart/tree.py', 'Stone 2 of the chart device', "that rung for chart's nexi"; (2) the docstring says a learning block needing a special adaptation subclasses the tool, and names OWNER = 'chart' as the default, which no live caller relies on once ticket 2b3d842bc118 is PROVED; (3) the charter's what and why say the same (one tool, users not an owner, subclass for an adaptation, outline 19.29); (4) behaviour unchanged: OWNER == 'chart', nexus_table('survey') == 'chart_survey_nodes', and cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py and test_questions.py stay green.

decisions.text: Red-first proof cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_the_tree_tool_names_itself_the_one_tool.py, check()/FAILURES/main() shape, one tooth per falsifier clause, PROVES = {'d23ca0e54d00': {'1':..,'4':..}} (tooth names written at build). Reads the docstring by ast.get_docstring and the charter as JSON; clause 4 imports the tool and calls nexus_table without touching the store.

Run the proof red, build, run it twice serially green plus the component's existing proofs. Commit before the hollow reading; seal with bin/cairn test --seal <path>.
